title: Dark Chocolate-Filled Soft Rolls
changes_from_base: Part wholemeal dough with milk powder and potato flakes, each roll folded around two sticks of dark chocolate.
summary: Pillowy sweet rolls folded around two sticks of dark chocolate and dusted with icing sugar.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel
baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: dark chocolate (70%), cut into 24 sticks about 8 cm long

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Combine all the dough ingredients, cover and leave 20 min, then knead until soft, smooth and slightly sticky. Oil your hands and the worktop rather than adding more flour.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave about 1 1/2 h, until puffy; it will not quite double but will lose most of its stickiness.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Halve the dough and roll each half on a lightly oiled worktop to a 20 x 23 cm rectangle. Cut each into 6 pieces of about 10 x 8 cm.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: With a short side facing you, lay a chocolate stick 2-3 cm from the far edge, fold that edge over it to the middle and press. Lay a second stick on the seam, then fold the near edge up over it and press again. Turn seam side down onto the tray and repeat, spacing the rolls 4 cm apart.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover and leave 1-1 1/2 h, until puffy. Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Brush with milk and bake 14-18 min, until light golden; the bread reads 88-93 °C. After 5 min move to a rack and dust with icing sugar. Serve warm, or rewarm briefly so the chocolate softens again.

tips: Oil the worktop instead of flouring it to keep the dough soft.
Cut the chocolate into neat sticks with a hot knife so it does not shatter.
Serve warm; rewarm leftovers briefly so the chocolate melts again.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight box for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 160 °C for 4-5 min; freeze for up to 1 month.
